hops.input_text: Negotiators from nearly 200 nations concluded two weeks of intensive multilateral negotiations early Sunday morning, reaching a historic consensus agreement to establish a dedicated financial mechanism for loss and damage assisting developing countries vulnerable to climate disruptions. The breakthrough came after continuous plenary sessions extending 36 hours past the official scheduled adjournment. Under the compromise framework, industrialized nations will contribute initial capital commitments to assist emerging economies facing economic destruction from sea-level rise, intensified droughts, and severe storm surges. However, contentious disagreements remain regarding which international financial institutions will oversee fund disbursements and whether emerging high-income economies will be classified as donor contributors.
